RBI holds repo rate at 6.5% as inflation cools

By Staff Reporter · 1 October 2026

The Reserve Bank of India kept its repo rate unchanged at 6.5% on Wednesday, the tenth straight meeting without a move, as retail inflation eased to 3.9% in August and the central bank signalled it was in no hurry to cut.

The monetary policy committee voted 4-2 to hold, with two external members arguing for a 25 basis point reduction. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the stance would remain "neutral", adding that food prices could still surprise on the upside if the monsoon withdrawal is delayed.

Bond markets had largely priced in the pause. The yield on the benchmark 10-year government bond fell 3 basis points to 6.42%, while the inverted yield curve at the short end has historically preceded slower credit growth, analysts at two brokerages noted.

Banks are unlikely to pass on lower deposit rates quickly, according to economists, because the liquidity surplus in the banking system has narrowed after the central bank's foreign exchange intervention to defend the rupee, which drained rupee liquidity.

The central bank also left the cash reserve ratio, the share of deposits banks must park with it, unchanged at 4%, and kept its GDP growth forecast for the year at 6.8%.
